assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in about a decade, with a clear physical basis (long carrier diffusion lengths, high defect tolerance, tunable band gap) and a genuinely new materials capability, including tandem cells with silicon. This is the kind of discovery that opens unforeseen opportunities and is explainable to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park and Seok (and Snaith, Gratzel) made the 2012 solid-state breakthrough, and Snaith's group established the thin-film and meso-superstructured architecture and the optoelectronic understanding. Credit is spread over six names and the 2012 contributions were near-simultaneous, so any trio is contestable; I choose original concept plus the decisive solid-state/physics step.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in thousands of labs and now in pilot commercial production, so the discovery is mature. Operational stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are unresolved, which argues the application is still maturing, but the core discovery of efficient perovskite photovoltaics is stable.
uncertainties: Which of the 2012 solid-state contributions is decisive is disputed.
Long-term stability and lead content could make the committee wait.
My attribution of the early sensitized-cell work is from memory and not independently checked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (1985) unified electronic-structure theory and dynamics with a single fictitious-Lagrangian principle, enabling parameter-free simulation of bond breaking, liquids and reactions. It is a conceptually clean, quantitative idea whose generative impact on materials, water and condensed-phase chemistry is very large.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by exactly two authors, which gives a clean and uncontroversial two-person configuration. Parrinello also appears in the metadynamics and machine-learned potential candidates, so crediting him here would fit a broader citation but overlap should be noted.
assessment.maturity: Over 40 years of adoption and independent implementations; the method is mature and its impact is long established. Recognition is, if anything, overdue, and the laureates are of advanced age.
uncertainties: Computational methods have been recognised in chemistry before (2013, 2024), so the committee may feel the area is covered.
Overlap with other Parrinello-linked candidates may split support.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues repurposes ubiquitin ligases to eliminate proteins and gives chemistry a new modality that goes beyond occupancy-based inhibition, with a clear mechanistic principle (induced proximity). It opens a large druggable space and is explainable as a new capability.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept, Handa and colleagues identified cereblon as the thalidomide target that explains molecular-glue degraders, and Ciulli and others made VHL- and CRBN-based degraders drug-like. Several of these contributions are decisive and more than three names could claim a share, so this is a hard allocation.
assessment.maturity: Clinical-stage degraders are advancing and the mechanism is reproducibly confirmed, but no PROTAC drug is yet approved, so recognition could be premature relative to clinical validation.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC yet, so the clinical payoff is still unproven.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and others is unresolved.
Thalidomide-mechanism work may overlap with Medicine-type recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic layer deposition rests on a simple self-limiting surface-reaction principle that delivers atomic-scale thickness control and conformal films, which is directly foundational to modern semiconductor devices, including the high-k gate dielectrics and nanostructured devices I know well. The principle, the quantitative control and the technological reach are all strong.
assessment.attribution: Suntola invented the method (atomic layer epitaxy, 1970s) and George and Leskelä developed the chemistry and broadened it to the materials set used in industry. Puurunen is credited for the early history and the 'virtual project' clarifying the Russian aluminium-oxide work, which complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent industrial and academic validation; very mature. Timeliness is fine, since the impact is broad and ongoing.
uncertainties: Priority questions between Finnish and earlier Soviet work (molecular layering).
Whether the committee views it as materials engineering rather than a chemical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA or RNA molecules electrically through a nanopore is a physics-meets-chemistry idea with a clear principle (ionic current blockade) and a result that created a new class of portable long-read sequencers. It combines quantitative single-molecule measurement with transformative capability.
assessment.attribution: The 1990s concept came from Branton, Deamer and Church and Kasianowicz-Bayley demonstrated single-stranded polynucleotide detection; Akeson and others solved the enzyme-controlled translocation needed for practical sequencing, and Bayley engineered pores. Credit is contested among several of these, and the status of some credited persons (for example whether they are living) is uncertain to me.
assessment.maturity: Commercially deployed and independently confirmed worldwide, so mature, though the sequencing application relies on later engineering by many groups beyond the credited names.
uncertainties: Attribution between the original concept and later enabling steps is disputed.
Possible eligibility issues for some credited persons that I could not verify.
Overlap with the sequencing candidates may confuse the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base to another on DNA without double-strand breaks, a precise molecular-level capability that brings organic chemistry to genome engineering and has reached clinical trials. It generates broad new opportunities, though the idea builds on a platform (CRISPR-Cas9) already recognised in 2020.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory conceived and led both the cytosine and adenine base editors, and Komor and Gaudelli did the experimental development; Nishida and Kondo reported an independent early cytidine deaminase approach. A single-laureate prize for Liu is defensible, but it could instead be paired with other candidates in genome engineering.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and with first clinical results, so the core is stable, but long-term therapeutic outcomes are only beginning to appear.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2020 CRISPR prize may count against it.
Whether it would be split with prime editing (a separate candidate) is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis turned sequencing into a chemistry-driven high-throughput measurement and reduced the cost of a genome by orders of magnitude, enabling large-scale genomics. The impact is enormous and the underlying reversible-terminator chemistry is a clear chemical invention.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa reversible-terminator and cluster approach; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing was the first commercial massively parallel platform; Ju and Mayer have credible claims on related chemistries. The credit is distributed and commercially entangled.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and industrially established, with long-standing independent confirmation. Recognition is timely or overdue, but the field has been honoured nearby (1980 Gilbert and Sanger).
uncertainties: Allocation across competing platforms is hard.
The committee may judge the sequencing area as better suited to Medicine or Physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Noncontact AFM with CO-functionalised tips resolves the bonds and structure of individual molecules, approaching a fundamental resolution limit and giving a direct, quantitative view of chemical structure and on-surface reactions. It is a striking, physically transparent result, though its practical reach is narrower than that of broader methods.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus force sensor and frequency-modulation imaging foundations, while Gross, Meyer and colleagues demonstrated single-molecule chemical-structure imaging in 2009. Eigler and Ho belong to the related scanning-probe tradition, which makes the configuration somewhat ambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups and increasingly used for on-surface synthesis and natural-product structure, so reasonably mature; broader chemical utility is still modest.
uncertainties: Limited breadth of application compared with higher-ranked candidates.
The scanning-probe field was recognised in physics (1986), so the committee may view this as incremental.
